cases.prompt: I'm using bBox_Python3Run in a FileMaker script to run a Python script, but when it fails I only get a '?' back with no useful detail. How do I get the actual error message?
expected: Identifies bBox_LastError(-3) as the correct reference parameter for bBox_Python3Run (from shared_reference.error_reference / the function's own error_reference field)
Recommends adding mode +32 to combine stdout & stderr, since Python's traceback goes to stderr and is otherwise discarded
Optionally references the worked example in the catalog: bBox_Python3Run(32; "y=5/0") & ¶ & bBox_LastError(-1) & ¶ & bBox_LastError(-3)

cases.prompt: I want to run a Bash script server-side (PSoS) that processes a file from a container field, and I also want to run a Python session (bBox_PythonCompile/Execute) at the same time in a different scheduled script. Any gotchas?
expected: Explains the container-field-reference mechanism for bBox_Bash: file is written to a temp bBox_file_XXXXXXXXX.bin path and substituted in as the parameter, purged after 3 days/reboot

Flags that bBox_PythonCompile/Execute/Eval are NOT thread or session safe — only one process-wide Python VM exists, so overlapping PSoS/schedule sessions using Python need a mutex/blocking mechanism, or should use bBox_Python3Run instead (thread safe, but no fm bridge)
Mentions the general PSoS caveat that GUI-dependent functions won't work server-side, and that stored calculation fields aren't reliable for Bash/Python-family functions
